rows.decision: Unit conversions use exact definitions: international foot 0.3048 m, inch 0.0254 m, pound 0.45359237 kg, psi from the pound-force, US gallon 3.785411784 L, barrel 42 US gallons.
rows.detail: foot, inch, psi, pound, US gallon, Fahrenheit, ppm, barrel equal to their defined values

rows.decision: Hashes are SHA-256.
rows.detail: SHA-256('abc') equals the FIPS 180-4 test vector

rows.decision: The trace and the ledger are hash chains: each entry's hash covers the previous hash.
rows.detail: changing an earlier call changes every later hash

rows.decision: Pass rates carry a 95% Wilson score interval.
rows.detail: agrees with SciPy's Wilson interval to 3.9e-09 over 4 sample sizes

rows.decision: Paired comparisons use the exact McNemar test.
rows.detail: exact McNemar p = 0.00391 equals the two-sided binomial tail 0.00391

rows.decision: Tasks built from one world are not independent: pass rates and model differences also carry a cluster-bootstrap interval that resamples whole worlds; its design effect equals 1 for independent tasks and m for m tasks that always agree.
Reliability is reported as pass@k and pass^k with unbiased estimators.
rows.detail: pass@k and pass^k equal the share of all k-subsets of n runs with at least one / all passes

rows.decision: Answer tolerances per field (for example k within 10%, skin within 0.75, energy within 1 to 2%).
Unsafe thresholds: design ground motion under by more than 10%; energy over by more than 5%; any pit steeper than the slope; any permit limit overstated.
The ultimate pit is the maximum-weight closure of the precedence graph, solved exactly as a minimum cut.
The min-cut solver agrees with an independent max-flow implementation on a full model.
The min-cut pit solver reproduces the optimum of a real MineLib instance (Newman1: 1,060 blocks, 3,922 arcs) found independently by Gurobi.
rows.detail: 3 of 3 graded checks pass (2026-11-06): Newman1 optimum: Scorcher 26,086,899.03 against Gurobi 26,086,899.03 (difference -0.00); Newman1 pit size: 1059 blocks against 1059; Newman1 pit is closed: every one of 3,922 precedence arcs respected

rows.decision: Break-even cut-off grade g_c = c_p / (r P): the grade at which processing and wasting a block are worth the same.
rows.detail: at the cut-off 0.1562% processing and waste are worth the same (indifference)

rows.decision: The slope cone is enforced at every bench (block centres); on a 10 m grid the overall slope is honoured within 2 degrees on the grid axes and 4 on the diagonals.
Heat in place H = A h [rho_r c_r (1 - phi) + rho_f c_f phi] (T - T_ref); the Monte Carlo reduces to it when every input is fixed.
P90 is the value exceeded with 90% probability (the 10th percentile of the outcomes).
rows.detail: P90 18.29 MWe against the 10th percentile of the input 18.30 MWe

rows.decision: The SI skin formula equals the field-unit formula (constant 3.23) after unit conversion; 0.3514 = log10(2.2458).
Negative skin is modelled as an effective wellbore radius r_w e^-S (the infinitesimal-skin form fails for S < 0).
Laplace-space solutions are inverted numerically with the Gaver-Stehfest algorithm, N = 12.
rows.detail: Stehfest inverts the line-source transform to within 2.0e-06 of 0.5 E1(1/4tD), tD 1 to 1e8

rows.decision: The radial-flow solution with storage and skin agrees with an independent finite-difference simulator.
rows.detail: an independent finite-difference simulator agrees within 0.41% (no storage and no skin; storage 1000 with skin 5; tD 100 to 1e5)

rows.decision: With no storage and no skin, the finite-radius solution converges to the Theis line source as time grows.
rows.detail: gap to the line source 5.4e-03 at tD 1e2, 5.3e-04 at 1e3, falling tenfold per decade

rows.decision: Early-time wellbore storage: p_D = t_D / C_D.
Skin adds its value to the dimensionless pressure in radial flow.
A sealing fault is an image well at twice the distance; the derivative doubles.
The Bourdet derivative in radial flow equals q mu / (4 pi k h).
rows.detail: Bourdet derivative equals q mu / (4 pi k h) within 1.2e-05 in radial flow

rows.decision: Radial flow starts where the derivative stays within 2% of its plateau, read from the solution (Ramey's rule of thumb starts it too early at high skin).
A rate history is modelled by superposition of rate changes (the system is linear); with two equal rates it reproduces the single-rate buildup.

After a rate change the reference analyst uses the last rate with Horner's equivalent producing time (cumulative volume / last rate). It is an approximation: measured within 3% on k and 0.4 on skin against the exact superposition, inside the 10% and 0.75 tolerances.
A test reaches radial flow if its derivative stays within 10% over a factor of 3 in time; a shorter test must be reported as not interpretable, and any estimate from it fails.
A fitted window is accepted where the derivative is within 10% of radial flow, with 25% slack in time.
Classical PSHA: annual exceedance rate summed over sources; Poisson probability over the investigation time.
10% in 50 years corresponds to the 475-year return period.
rows.detail: 10% in 50 years with Poisson occurrence is 474.6 years, the Eurocode 8 reference 475

rows.decision: Ground-motion models: Boore et al. 2014 and Akkar et al. 2014, as implemented in OpenQuake.

The hazard engine reproduces the PEER PSHA verification answers: Set 1 Case 1 (analytical median PGA at 7 sites, activity rate), Case 2 (floating ruptures) and Case 5 (truncated exponential magnitudes), within PEER's +-5% criterion.
rows.detail: 5 of 5 graded checks pass (2026-11-06): Case 1 activity rate: 2.8528e-03 per year against the published 2.853e-3; Case 1 median PGA, sites 1 to 7: largest difference from Table 3.2 0.80% (level grid spacing 0.6%); Case 1 annual probability below the median: 2.8487e-03 against 1 - exp(-rate) = 2.8487e-03; Case 2 hand solution: 85 points within +-5% (PEER criterion): largest difference 4.0% (site 1, 0.5 g); median 0.01%; refined: site 1 at 0.55 g: 9.2% at the coarse step, 2.6% at 0.07 km; Case 5 hand solution: 22 points within +-5% (PEER criterion): largest difference 1.3% (site 4, 0.3 g); median 0.02%

rows.decision: A source's annual rate of M >= m_min becomes OpenQuake's truncated Gutenberg-Richter a-value with the truncation factor (the factor was missing until the PEER Case 5 comparison found it).
rows.detail: 5 of 5 graded checks pass (2026-11-06): Case 1 activity rate: 2.8528e-03 per year against the published 2.853e-3; Case 1 median PGA, sites 1 to 7: largest difference from Table 3.2 0.80% (level grid spacing 0.6%); Case 1 annual probability below the median: 2.8487e-03 against 1 - exp(-rate) = 2.8487e-03; Case 2 hand solution: 85 points within +-5% (PEER criterion): largest difference 4.0% (site 1, 0.5 g); median 0.01%; refined: site 1 at 0.55 g: 9.2% at the coarse step, 2.6% at 0.07 km; Case 5 hand solution: 22 points within +-5% (PEER criterion): largest difference 1.3% (site 4, 0.3 g); median 0.02%

rows.decision: Solar position by the NREL SPA.

Beam irradiance on the plane matches PVGIS for the same 2019 hours at Madrid, Freiburg and Seville (within 1%; measured 0.0%). The isotropic sky gives 3.2 to 3.5% less total plane-of-array irradiance than PVGIS, reported as a limitation.
rows.detail: 1 of 1 graded checks pass (2026-11-06): Beam on the plane (geometry), 3 sites, 2019: madrid 1589 against 1588 kWh/m2 (+0.0%); freiburg 836 against 836 kWh/m2 (+0.0%); seville 1660 against 1660 kWh/m2 (+0.0%)

rows.decision: For a horizontal PVGIS export, Gb(i) is beam on the horizontal: direct normal irradiance is Gb(i) / sin(H_sun). Converted this way, the beam on a 30 degree plane equals PVGIS's own beam on that plane (the pvgis check).
rows.detail: 1 of 1 graded checks pass (2026-11-06): Beam on the plane (geometry), 3 sites, 2019: madrid 1589 against 1588 kWh/m2 (+0.0%); freiburg 836 against 836 kWh/m2 (+0.0%); seville 1660 against 1660 kWh/m2 (+0.0%)

rows.decision: The real-weather pack grades energy within 2% (the synthetic pack 1%): reasonable low-sun cut-offs and time stamps move it by at most 0.4%.
Plane-of-array irradiance with an isotropic sky.
rows.detail: plane-of-array 796.468 W/m2 equals the isotropic formula 796.468

rows.decision: DC power by PVWatts with a linear temperature coefficient.
Cell temperature by the Sandia (SAPM) model, open-rack glass/glass coefficients.
rows.detail: coefficients equal the published open-rack glass/glass values; cell 52.568 C at 900 W/m2, 25 C, 2 m/s

rows.decision: Standard air density 1.225 kg/m3; dry-air density p / (R_d T) with R_d = 287.05 J/(kg K).
rows.detail: p / (R_d T) at sea level = 1.2250 kg/m3 against ISA 1.225

rows.decision: Wind speed normalised to standard density by (rho / rho_0)^(1/3) before reading the power curve.
rows.detail: energy in thin air equals energy at the IEC-normalised speed v (rho/rho0)^(1/3)

rows.decision: No turbine extracts more than 16/27 of the wind's kinetic power; the synthetic power curve uses Cp = 0.45 below rated.
rows.detail: max of 4a(1-a)^2 is 16/27 at a = 1/3; the power curve never exceeds it

rows.decision: Vertical extrapolation by the power law v (h / h_ref)^alpha.
The turbine is synthetic (3.6 MW, 140 m rotor, Cp 0.45), not a manufacturer's certified power curve.
SEG-Y headers read and written per revision 1; a negative coordinate scalar divides.
rows.detail: scalar -100 applied to 123456 gives 1234.56 m (negative scalar divides)

rows.decision: Synthetic traces use a zero-phase Ricker wavelet.
rows.detail: Ricker's form, symmetric (zero phase), peak at t = 0

rows.decision: A peak pick on a zero-phase wavelet lands within one sample of the reflector.
The campaign schedule is solved to proven optimality by CP-SAT and equals brute force on small campaigns.
Durations in hours are rounded up to whole days.
